title: Normalized signed totalization on chosen finite-projective resolutions
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism on the small pro-etale sites, let $R_Y,R_X$ be commutative ring sheaves, and fix $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Use the ordinary uncompleted module derived categories and canonical module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the normalized K-flat tensor comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and cochain localization $\mathcal Q_T$ on $T=X,Y$. Let $K\in D(R_X)$, $P\in D(R_Y)$, choose a K-injective complex $I^\bullet$ with $\alpha:K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q_XI^\bullet$, and a bounded complex $F^\bullet$ with $\beta:\mathcal Q_YF^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}P$. For each degree $r$, supply a strict-perfect package $F^r\xrightarrow{i_r}R_Y^{N_r}\xrightarrow{p_r}F^r$, $p_ri_r=1$, as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package].

Set $C=\operatorname{Tot}(f_*I\otimes F)$, $J=\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes f^*F)$ and $B=f_*J$, using differential $d_I\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_F$ in bidegree $(a,r)$. Let $t:C\to B$ be the ordinary signed total counit mate, and $s:B\to C$ the degreewise retract inverse specified in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. Thus the $(a,r)$ summand of $s$ is $(1\otimes p_r)q_{I^a,N_r}f_*(1\otimes f^*i_r)$, with $q_{I^a,N_r}$ the inverse of the ordinary finite-free projection identification. Write $\eta_H:\mathcal Q_Y(f_*H)\to Rf_*\mathcal Q_XH$ for the right-derived comparison, $\ell_F:Lf^*\mathcal Q_YF\cong\mathcal Q_X(f^*F)$ for exact pullback comparison, and $m_Y,m_X$ for the canonical mixed tensor comparisons with coefficient complexes $F,f^*F$.

Then $F$ and $f^*F$ are flat-term K-flat complexes and $J$ is K-injective. In particular $\eta_I,\eta_J$ and the following specified comparisons are isomorphisms:
$$S=m_Y\circ((\eta_I^{-1}\circ Rf_*\alpha)\otimes\beta^{-1}):Rf_*K\otimes^LP\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q_YC,$$
$$T=\eta_J^{-1}\circ Rf_*\bigl(m_X\circ(\alpha\otimes(\ell_F\circ Lf^*\beta^{-1}))\bigr):Rf_*(K\otimes^LLf^*P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q_YB.$$
For the canonical derived counit projection mate $\pi_{f,K,P}$, the adjunct of $(\varepsilon_K\otimes1)\mu_{Rf_*K,P}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], one has
$$\pi_{f,K,P}=T^{-1}\circ\mathcal Q_Y(t)\circ S,$$
and $S^{-1}\circ\mathcal Q_Y(s)\circ T$ is its two-sided inverse. These equalities hold for every choice of $I,F,\alpha,\beta$ and every degreewise splitting package; no boundedness of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply proEtaleStrictPerfect_flat from [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] to the supplied bounded coefficient package. For the pulled-back complex, transport the inclusion and retraction by the exact additive module pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. PreservesProduct.iso followed by the product of the uniquely characterized pullback-unit isomorphism identifies the image finite free object with the corresponding finite free object on X. Functoriality preserves the splitting equation, including rank zero. Additivity sends the zero terms outside the given bounds to zero. Apply proEtaleStrictPerfect_flat again to this transported package. This proves the two flat-term K-flat assertions without choosing any new resolution.

source.place: Second paragraph, bounded strict-perfect coefficients and termwise pullback.

proof.text: Apply tensorAdjunctionTotal_target_isKInjective from [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] to the exact module pullback, its pullback-unit isomorphism, the given K-injective I and the bounded coefficient splitting. This theorem proves K-injectivity of the target total by the triangulated right-orthogonal criterion; it imposes no bound on I and no chain-map condition on the splitting. The canonical K-injective comparison theorem proEtaleRingDerivedDirectImage_kInjective in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] then makes eta_I and eta_J invertible. This completes model_properties.

source.place: Second paragraph, K-injective target total and derived comparisons.

proof.text: Use the specified mixed comparisons from [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] and the exact pullback comparison to form S and T, exactly as in their unchanged definitions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-mixed-projection-mate] at I and F with the just-proved flat K-flat assertion. Its ordinary total map is definitionally totalMate. Postcompose the resulting equality with eta_J inverse to obtain (eta_I tensor identity) followed by pi at QI,QF and the normalized target comparison equals m_Y followed by Q(t). The mixed-mate theorem already supplies the localization normalization, so no additional fixed-tensor descent proof is needed here.

source.place: Second paragraph, normalized signed total mate; Stacks 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map.

proof.text: Transport that equality along alpha and beta inverse. Naturality of the existing rightAdjointProjectionMap in both arguments is naturality of the canonical mate specified by [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Precompose by tensor of eta_I inverse and cancel eta_I. Tensor functoriality combines the representative changes with the normalized comparisons, giving precisely S and T. The proved private transport_projection lemma performs this categorical calculation. Cancel T to obtain pi = S.hom followed by Q(t) followed by T.inv for arbitrary derived representative isomorphisms.

source.place: Third paragraph, independence of the chosen representatives.

proof.text: The existing tensorAdjunctionTotal_isIso theorem of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], applied to the uniquely normalized pullback unit and the bounded degreewise splitting, makes totalMate invertible. By definition totalInverse is its inverse, whose finite-total retract summands are already characterized by tensorAdjunctionTotalInverse_summand. Substitute the forward formula and the unchanged definition of inverse. Cancel the source and target model isomorphisms, combine adjacent localization maps using functoriality, and localize the two ordinary inverse equations. This proves both displayed identity equations. All steps apply also when F is zero or its degreewise ranks are zero, and require no boundedness of I.
